The doubtful assumption is the page helper input envelope, not clone isolation. mainHost.request records the full HTTP response but returns envelope.Data; mainHost.ok returns that already-unwrapped payload. R3 physically returned the source-exact VAlert and config{} for AutoSignIncopy. Its nested-data helper discarded Page to nil, so the failure text incorrectly accused inherited history. The same helper would misclassify reset later. The only confirmed required patch is attached in empty-page-helper.diff: decode a top-level Page and compare got.Page. No Root driver, true source, SDK, old failure or binary is modified; no new Go/App build or Main run occurs.

## Proof-strength details, not new demonstrated product defects

The existing successful-row helper's first dot uses the known source first-column=today layout and only checks a title suffix, and its1/1 summary scan is not tied to the 今日签到 label. It is adequate for the observed one-site row fixture but should not be described as an independent calendar/date or all-summary-fields check. If that broader claim is desired, use source `_date_label` and bind1/1 to the same stat item as 今日签到, then preflight those helpers offline before another Main attempt.

Cleanup registration currently records peer observations before mainHost's cleanup stops the host; deferred peer.Close also runs before t.Cleanup. This is not the R3 cause. For a complete physical-observation lifetime, use t.Cleanup(peer.Close) before newMainHost, and in the later owned cleanup call h.stop before copying/recording seen. Existing h.stop cleanup is idempotent and will then only close events. Keep failure raw and classify this as test evidence hygiene, not a product change.

After three attempts, do not blindly retry. First validate the minimal corrected helper offline against the saved unwrapped response, the full-envelope negative case, missing/null/wrong shapes and altered alert fields. offline-envelope-replay.json does exactly that using six negative controls, without Go compilation or actual Main execution. Parent can review and then deliberately choose the next actual gate. Existing r1/r2/r3 failures must remain immutable and uncounted as complete acceptance.
